input: My landlord in Koramangala cut off the water supply 3 days ago because I complained about the rent hike. What can I do?

intake.english_summary: Tenant reports landlord cut off water supply 3 days ago after complaint about rent hike; seeks guidance.

timeline.event: water supply cut off by landlord

missing_info: Do you have a written lease agreement?
Has the landlord provided any notice before cutting off the water?
Is the water supply part of the rent or a separate utility?

answer.where_you_stand: Your landlord cut off water, an essential supply, without just and sufficient cause. This breaches Section 49 of the Karnataka Rent Act [KRA-s49-p1].
options: Apply to the Rent Controller under Section 49(2) for an order to restore water immediately (interim order) [KRA-s49-p1].
Ask the Controller to direct the landlord to pay compensation for the wrongful cut‑off [KRA-s49-p1].
Seek penalty against the landlord under Section 54 for the offence (fine up to three months’ rent and Rs 100 per day of default) [KRA-s54-p3].
next_steps: Gather evidence: dates, photos, any written communication about the rent hike and water cut‑off.
Prepare a written application to the Controller stating the facts and that the cut‑off was to force you to pay higher rent.
Submit the application with supporting documents and request an interim order for immediate restoration of water.
Attend the Controller’s inquiry, present your case, and ask for compensation and penalty.
If the landlord does not comply with the order, inform the Controller to enforce the fine and daily penalty.
answer.what_i_dont_know: The exact terms of your rental agreement, any prior written notice from the landlord, and whether you have already lodged a formal complaint with the landlord.
answer.lawyer_reason: Preparing and filing the application with the Rent Controller and presenting evidence can be technical; a lawyer can help draft the petition and represent you at the hearing.

verdicts.reason: Section 49(1) prohibits a landlord from cutting off essential supplies like water without just cause; the facts show the landlord cut off water, so it breaches the provision.
Section 49(2) allows the tenant to apply to the Controller, and Section 49(3) permits an interim order to restore the supply immediately, matching the suggested action.
Section 49(5) empowers the Controller to direct compensation (up to Rs 50) to the tenant when the landlord withholds essential supply without just cause.
Section 54(ix) provides a penalty for contravening Section 49(1), including a fine up to three months' rent and Rs 100 per day of default, so the tenant may seek such penalty.
